_comment: Ceilings for scripts/bench-memory.sh, checked when BENCH_THRESHOLDS points here (CI does). Units: KiB. core_on re-seeded 2026-09-03 after the Round 4/5 merges (52b0a67) at ~20% above the gate run (serve+first 5.19 MiB, per empty 0.12 MiB, per filled 0.39 MiB / 0.30 after 10 s idle, per client 1 KiB, core 6.4–8.3 MiB after teardown across runs, ceiling 10500); core_off rows keep their Round 2 seeds. The core is the default since 0.4.4: an unset UNPEEL_PTY_CORE infers the core_on profiles. Tighten as rounds land, never loosen without a note here. 'leftover_hosts' and 'leftover_dirs' are exact: reclamation must be total. 'vt_empty_grid_kib'/'vt_filled_grid_kib' are the in-process libghostty-vt grid rows (BENCH_VT=1, CI) measured against the vendored small-page build; 'per_client_kib' is exact bytes (footprint -f bytes). 2026-09-03 evening: core_on per_filled (480→650) and core_after_teardown (10500→21000) reseeded at ~20% above the hosted macOS CI runner's first clean run (523 KiB / 17.1 MiB) — CI-runner allocator/page behaviour, not a regression; local numbers stay 0.30–0.44 MiB and 6.3–8.3 MiB. serve_plus_first_session stays 6400 now that the engine download streams to disk and the bench opts out of the install (UNPEEL_BROWSER_ENGINE_INSTALL=0).

linux_core_off._comment: Linux rows are PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup (shared library pages count proportionally, so (a) is ~14 MiB where macOS phys_footprint says ~5); seeded 2026-09-03 (Round 4, Lane 3) at 20% above the first real run: rust:1.88-bullseye arm64 container on Apple silicon, release binaries, small-page libghostty-vt Linux slices, unpeel-attach via epoll+inotify.

linux_core_on._comment: Linux rows are PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup (shared library pages count proportionally, so (a) is ~14 MiB where macOS phys_footprint says ~5); seeded 2026-09-03 (Round 4, Lane 3) at 20% above the first real run: rust:1.88-bullseye arm64 container on Apple silicon, release binaries, small-page libghostty-vt Linux slices, unpeel-attach via epoll+inotify. 2026-09-03 evening: core_after_teardown 10000→13500 after the first clean ubuntu-latest run settled at 10.99 MiB (container seed was 8.13 MiB); every other Linux row was inside its ceiling (per empty 0.04 MiB, per filled 0.42, per client 20 KiB). 2026-09-04: core_after_teardown 13500→18000 — ubuntu-latest settles anywhere from 9.3 to 15.1 MiB run to run on the same commit (glibc trim on a 2-core runner), so this row is a leak guard, not a precision gate; the per-session rows carry the precision.
